title: Temporal mix sculptor with bounded-tail oscillation detector
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Synthetic workload runners at the benchmark lab have historically focused on either purely stochastic mixes or long-running steady-state traces. Teams asked for a compact, configurable runner that can express temporally varying mixes (ramp/hold/spike patterns) with guarantees about tail behaviour so that profiling baselines are repeatable. This PR introduces the Temporal Mix Sculptor: a workload generator that composes named phases (delay, ramp, hold, burst, decay) into a timeline and emits request sequences with controllable concurrency, sequence length mix, and token distributions.

Key features implemented: bounded-tail oscillation detector (BTOD) — a lightweight online detector that flags microburst oscillations and produces an oscillation_score per epoch (0..1) so that downstream reports can disambiguate pathological tail events from steady-state variance; epochal histogram summarizer — compact per-epoch histograms (fixed 256 buckets) using reservoir+count-min sketch hybrid to bound memory for long runs; temporal policy DSL — a small declarative YAML schema to describe multi-phase mixes and deterministic seeds for reproducible runs; per-request trace IDs and KV-cache priming options so runs can model warm/cold starts.

Why this matters: several recent perf investigations required isolating oscillatory tail events from steady high-p95s when validating kernel changes. The BTOD score is intended to be surfaced as a top-level dimension in reports (oscillation: true/false and score) and to drive automatic run reclassification in the reporting pipeline. The smaller histograms enable nightlies to retain useful distributional information without exploding storage costs.

Commits summary: single-squash merge with a sequence of focused commits during review: initial scaffold and DSL, core runner loop and phase engine, BTOD algorithm and tests, histogram summarizer and exporter, telemetry/trace id plumbing, unit/integration tests and small CI fixes.

Files changed (high-level):
- benchmark-lab/runner/temporal_sculptor.py (core runner + DSL parser)
- benchmark-lab/telemetry/btod.py (oscillation detector, unit tested)
- benchmark-lab/reporting/histogram_exporter.go (compact export for nightly reports)
- benchmark-lab/examples/scenarios/ci-temporal-mix.yaml (example policies)
- benchmark-lab/tests/test_temporal_sculptor.py (unit + integration harness)
- benchmark-lab/tests/data/sample_sequences.json (sample sequences for regression)
- benchmark-lab/benchmarks/daily_workloads.yaml (registration for nightly pipeline)
- benchmark-lab/README.md (docs + usage)
- CHANGES.md (entry)

Testing and CI: Local unit and integration test suite added. Initial CI run failed due to an interaction between the Go exporter lint rules and the CI container; fixed by pinning gofmt version and adjusting module path. Final CI state: all checks passed (unit, integration, linters).

Backward compatibility and safety: Runner defaults to the existing 'steady' profile unless a temporal policy is supplied. The histogram exporter adds a new compact endpoint but does not remove or change any existing exports. No breaking changes to public interfaces.

Release notes: Adds a new Temporal Mix Sculptor workload generator (benchmark-lab) with oscillation detection and compact histogram exports to improve regression triage for tail events.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice approach — the BTOD algorithm is compact and the score makes sense. Two requests: add an integration test that reproduces a synthetic oscillation and assert the score crosses 0.7, and document the default seed behaviour.

Maya Chen: Added an integration harness in test_temporal_sculptor.py that flips an injected workload generator into oscillation mode and asserts a BTOD score > 0.75. Also expanded README with seed docs.

Sofia Patel: Can we avoid adding a hard dependency on count-min in the reporting binary? Prefer a vendored tiny implementation or a pure-Go sketch. Also comment about bucket alignment when sequences have long tail lengths.
Maya Chen: Switched to a minimal in-repo sketch implementation and aligned buckets to power-of-two boundaries; added notes in histogram_exporter.go explaining tradeoffs.
Ravi Kumar: CI flakes on mac runners observed previously — tests that read system timezone can break. Suggest forcing TZ in integration harness.
Maya Chen: Forced TZ=UTC in the harness setup; re-ran CI. All checks green.
merge_commit_message: Temporal mix sculptor: add phase-based workload runner, BTOD, histogram exporter and docs (squash)
release_notes: New benchmark: temporal mix sculptor with bounded-tail oscillation detection and compact per-epoch histogram exports. Useful for nightly regression triage of tail events.
